features.name: contraction_rate_oc
features.definition: What proportion of words across the counter-argument comments are contractions (e.g., I'm, don't, isn't)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads (malformed/missing -> null). Concatenate all comment strings; empty list -> null. Normalize curly apostrophes (’) to '. Words = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]+(?:'[A-Za-z]+)*", text). Contractions = words matching case-insensitive r"^[A-Za-z]+(?:n't|'m|'re|'ve|'ll|'d)$" or the specific forms it's, that's, what's, there's, here's, he's, she's, let's, who's, where's, how's (other 's treated as possessive and not counted); also can't, won't, ain't, y'all. Value = contraction count / total word count (null if zero words). Raw text count: includes any quoted text in comments and any outcome announcements; no semantic filtering.

h0: contraction_rate_oc has no association with delta.
h1: Higher contraction_rate_oc is associated with lower likelihood of delta (view change).
note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view). Contraction use is measured as a rate per word (normalizing for length), an operational assumption; the hypothesis says "more contractions" without specifying count vs rate. Pooled across all OC_comments; list order and individual commenters unknown. Contractions are a proxy for informality; the "formal language more persuasive" interpretation is not separately measured. Possessive 's excluded by assumption. Raw text may contain outcome announcements or quotes of others; not filtered. Association only, not causal.
